subject: Maths
title: Non-Linear Simultaneous Equations
subtitle: Simultaneous Equations · GCSE Higher (Grade 8–9)
learning_objective: Solve a pair of equations where one is linear (a straight line) and one is non-linear (a quadratic or a circle), using substitution. Recognise that there are usually two solution points and find both x values with their matching y values.

key_vocab.definition: Two or more equations that are true at the same time; the solution is the point(s) where they meet.
Replacing one variable using one equation so the other equation has a single unknown.
An equation whose graph is a curve (e.g. a quadratic or a circle) rather than a straight line.
An exact answer left with a root sign, e.g. (−1 + √17)/2, rather than a rounded decimal.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: Solve a pair of equations where one is a straight line (linear) and one is a curve (quadratic or circle) using substitution. Most pairs have two answer points — find both x values and the y that goes with each. Write each answer as a coordinate (x, y).

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content:
Simultaneous equations — equations that are true at the same time; the solution is where the graphs meet.
Substitution — replacing y (or x) using one equation so the other has a single unknown.
Non-linear — an equation whose graph is a curve (quadratic or circle).
Surd form — an exact answer left with a root sign, e.g. (−1 + √17)/2.

sections.title: Method — Five Steps
sections.content:
Step 1: Make y (or x) the subject of the straight-line equation.
Step 2: Substitute that into the non-linear equation.
Step 3: Move everything to one side so it equals 0.
Step 4: Solve the quadratic — factorise or use the formula.
Step 5: Put each value back to find its pair. Write answers as (x, y) and check.

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Solve:  y = x² − 2x + 3   and   y = x + 3

Substitute:  x² − 2x + 3 = x + 3
Rearrange:   x² − 3x = 0
Factorise:   x(x − 3) = 0  →  x = 0  or  x = 3
Find y:      x = 0 → y = 3;   x = 3 → y = 6
Answers:     (0, 3)  and  (3, 6)

sections.title: Question 1
frame: Both equations already give y, so set them equal:  x² = 2x + 3
Move everything to one side so it equals 0:  x² − 2x − 3 = 0
Factorise and solve to find the two x values.
Put each x back into y = 2x + 3 to find its y.
sections.content:
Solve the simultaneous equations.

   y = x²            and            y = 2x + 3

sections.title: Question 2
frame: Set the two right-hand sides equal, then rearrange to = 0.
Factorise to find the two x values, then find each matching y.
sections.content:
Solve the simultaneous equations.

   y = x² + 1        and        y = x + 3

sections.title: Question 3
sections.content:
Solve the simultaneous equations.

   y = x² − 2x       and        y = x + 4

sections.title: Question 4
sections.content:
Solve the simultaneous equations.

   y = x² − 5x + 6     and     y = x − 2

sections.title: Question 5
sections.content:
Solve the simultaneous equations.

   x² + y² = 25       and       y = x − 1

sections.title: Question 6
sections.content:
Solve the simultaneous equations.

   x² + y² = 10       and       x + y = 4

sections.title: Question 7
sections.content:
Solve the simultaneous equations. Give your answers in surd form.

   x² + y² = 9        and        y = x + 1

sections.title: Question 8
sections.content:
A rectangle has an area of 12 cm² and a perimeter of 14 cm.

By forming and solving a pair of simultaneous equations, find the length and width of the rectangle.

(Let the length be x and the width be y.)

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✗ There are usually TWO answers, not one — find both x values (e.g. x = 3 and x = −1).
✗ Get everything on one side so it equals 0 first: x² = 2x + 3 becomes x² − 2x − 3 = 0.
✗ Watch the minus signs: (x − 1)² = x² − 2x + 1, not x² − 1.
✗ Each x has its own y — after finding x, substitute back to find the matching y.

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award method marks for a correct substitution and rearrangement to = 0, and accuracy marks for both coordinate pairs.

Q1 (3):  (3, 9) and (−1, 1)
Q2 (3):  (2, 5) and (−1, 2)
Q3 (3):  (4, 8) and (−1, 3)
Q4 (3):  (4, 2) and (2, 0)
Q5 (4):  (4, 3) and (−3, −4)
Q6 (4):  (1, 3) and (3, 1)
Q7 (5):  x = (−1 + √17)/2, y = (1 + √17)/2  and  x = (−1 − √17)/2, y = (1 − √17)/2
Q8 (5):  length 4 cm, width 3 cm  (from xy = 12 and x + y = 7)

Total: 30 marks.
